methodology.rule: Research priority is not V10 Thesis Score. >=7 requires thesis-specific public evidence beyond the sparse YC tagline.

items.name: CharacterQuilt
items.tagline: Computer use agents to deploy enterprise marketing campaigns
items.why: Enterprise marketing execution has direct budget displacement. Public YC/job material says revenue grew from $1.5M to $3.5M during the batch, a $13M seed, and customers including Asana/Follett launching campaigns far faster.
items.what_can_kill: Services intensity, enterprise implementation and computer-use reliability could cap margins.

items.name: AutoSitu
items.tagline: The AI operating system for the built world
items.why: Strong buyer/workflow plus unusually strong public usage evidence: 25k+ developments analyzed, $18B+ development value, named public/private customers, and multiple monetizable steps from feasibility to construction.
items.what_can_kill: Long enterprise/public-sector sales cycles and local code/entitlement complexity.

items.name: DiligenceSquared
items.tagline: AI-powered market due diligence for investment decisions
items.why: High-ticket incumbent spend is explicit: PE funds pay $500k-$1M for diligence; company claims 5 of top 10 PE funds and $3T+ combined client AUM. Clear economic replacement wedge.
items.what_can_kill: Human-consultant layer may remain necessary and limit software margins/scale.

items.name: Openroll
items.tagline: The AI workforce for People and Finance teams
items.why: Named enterprise customers and recurring People/Finance workflows. Public customer material includes Notion, Flock Safety, Viaplay and measurable replacement of spreadsheet analysis.
items.what_can_kill: Crowded HR/FP&A category and enterprise integration burden.

items.name: InstaAgent
items.tagline: Scale marketing campaigns across hundreds of personas
items.why: Company reports $1M ARR in 10 months, 500+ clients and performance improvement claims. Buyer, acquisition budget and feedback loop are explicit.
items.what_can_kill: Agency-heavy delivery, creative quality churn and platform dependency.

items.name: transload
items.tagline: Measure freight with security cameras
items.why: Very crisp value capture: company reports ~15% of shipments larger than declared and ~$50k/site/month opportunity from rebillings and utilization using existing cameras.
items.what_can_kill: Computer-vision accuracy, hardware/camera variability and enterprise deployment friction.

items.name: Arden
items.tagline: AI-native internal audit firm
items.why: Mandatory SOX workflow with public-company budgets. YC says SOX can cost ~$2M/year, 70%+ labor, with consultants at $500-$1,000/hour. Strong risk/mandatory engine.
items.what_can_kill: Audit liability, integration breadth and incumbent GRC platforms.

items.name: Tepali
items.tagline: AI EMR for medspas & wellness clinics
items.why: Vertical all-in-one with direct revenue/admin claims: +53% leads booked, 68+ admin hours/month back and $14k+ additional monthly revenue per location.
items.what_can_kill: Healthcare/EMR compliance and crowded practice-management incumbents.

items.name: Dayjob
items.tagline: AI Scheduling for Short Haul Trucks
items.why: Specific operational wedge with measurable benefit: YC says customers in waste management see 8%+ efficiency gains from day one.
items.what_can_kill: ERP/TMS integration and dispatch exception handling can dominate implementation.

items.name: Signals
items.tagline: iMessage revenue channel for DTC brands that brings customers back
items.why: A/B-tested value claim directly tied to revenue: ~$30 average incremental repeat revenue per iMessage conversation.
items.what_can_kill: Apple/channel dependency, deliverability policy and DTC concentration.

items.name: 21st
items.tagline: UI building blocks for the agentic internet
items.why: Large demonstrated developer distribution: YC reports ~2M developers/1.4M+ registry users plus agent deployment infrastructure.
items.what_can_kill: Open-source commoditization and hyperscalers absorbing deployment primitives.

items.name: Overshoot
items.tagline: AI Infra for real-time vision applications
items.why: Technical benchmark + developer adoption: <200ms real-time vision claim and hundreds/1000+ developers cited publicly.
items.what_can_kill: Inference platform competition and model providers improving native streaming video.

items.name: Stilta
items.tagline: Agentic AI for intellectual property
items.why: High-stakes patent workflow, 50+ IP teams publicly claimed and $10.5M financing. Buyer and costly manual substitute are clear.
items.what_can_kill: Legal accuracy/liability and professional trust barrier.

items.name: Khotan (formerly Pollinate)
items.tagline: FDE as a platform for rebuilding critical operations in software.
items.why: YC reports customers spending ~40% of time on manual operations and $100k+ purchasing volume already processed through automated workflows.
items.what_can_kill: FDE/custom work can become consulting and make deployments non-repeatable.

items.name: Revnu
items.tagline: Your AI growth hire.
items.why: Published $1,500/month pricing and full execution across paid/outbound/SEO create a direct comparison with a growth hire/agency.
items.what_can_kill: Extremely crowded GTM market and attribution/churn risk.

items.name: Wideframe
items.tagline: AI coworker for video editors to ship more video faster
items.why: Clear $100/month/seat pricing and workflow-level time replacement for professional editors; team expansion path is explicit.
items.what_can_kill: Adobe/creative incumbents can bundle preparation features.

items.name: The Hog
items.tagline: Real-time web intelligence API for AI agents and GTM teams
items.why: Published API pricing, concrete replacement set (search/scraping/enrichment/monitoring) and benchmark claims create measurable developer economics.
items.what_can_kill: Data-provider dependence and intense search/enrichment competition.

items.name: Metorial
items.tagline: Agentic infrastructure to power AI-native companies.
items.why: Clear enterprise MCP/integration layer with 1,000+ integrations and governance/access-control wedge.
items.what_can_kill: MCP infrastructure is crowded and platform vendors can absorb integration/governance.

items.name: Deep Interactions
items.tagline: Collaborative AI app builder for teams
items.why: YC reports 12 businesses and 50k+ real-world usage hits; service-to-product wedge attacks expensive AI pilot failure.
items.what_can_kill: May remain bespoke delivery/consulting instead of scalable software.

items.name: Balance
items.tagline: Full-Stack AI Accounting
items.why: Very clear SMB payer and recurring monthly-close workflow; full outsourced-finance positioning enables value capture beyond a point tool.
items.what_can_kill: Human review requirement and accounting liability could compress margins.

items.name: Burt
items.tagline: AI teammates for logistics
items.why: Freight brokers/forwarders are explicit buyers; workload includes tracking, documents, carrier booking, invoicing and reconciliation with headcount economics.
items.what_can_kill: Razor-thin broker margins and deep TMS integration.

items.name: Haladir
items.tagline: Operational Superintelligence for Global Logistics
items.why: Combines solver-grade optimization with execution agents over WMS/TMS/ERP; raised $4.3M and targets high-value logistics operations.
items.what_can_kill: Custom integration intensity and long enterprise implementations.

items.name: LinkLane
items.tagline: AI-powered freight brokerage. Quote, book, and track loads in seconds.
items.why: End-to-end quote/book/track workflow and transactional monetization; clear shipper value. Brazil gains an additional local wedge from CIOT/piso-frete workflows.
items.what_can_kill: Brokerage margin/liquidity and regulatory/local carrier operations.

items.name: FullSeam
items.tagline: AI agents for corporate accounting teams
items.why: Clear corporate accounting buyer and repetitive AP/AR/reconciliation work outside ERP.
items.what_can_kill: ERP/accounting suites can absorb workflow agents and enterprise controls slow deployment.

items.name: BentoLabs AI
items.tagline: Monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents
items.why: Production-agent reliability is a real operational cost; founders cite experience at 5M-user agents and company claims production use with unicorns.
items.what_can_kill: Observability/agent-platform vendors can converge on the same feature set.

items.name: Terminal Use
items.tagline: AI-native transformation for operations-heavy companies
items.why: Starts with one measurable process and sells transformation into operations-heavy companies; strong FDE pedigree.
items.what_can_kill: Consulting intensity and long transformation cycles.

items.name: Asendia AI
items.tagline: AI recruiters for staffing agencies
items.why: Explicit staffing-agency buyer and throughput metric: screen more candidates and deliver shortlists faster without adding recruiter headcount.
items.what_can_kill: Crowded recruiting-agent market and candidate-quality risk.

items.name: Callab AI
items.tagline: AI voice agents for on-prem telephony stack.
items.why: On-prem PBX/SIP integration and live supervision differentiate it from cloud-only voice agents; clear contact-center buyer.
items.what_can_kill: Telephony integrations, compliance and crowded voice-agent market.

items.name: Vela
items.tagline: AI Recruiting Coordinator for Executive Search
items.why: Narrow scheduling wedge with no new dashboard/workflow and obvious recruiter-coordinator time replacement.
items.what_can_kill: Calendar/email platforms can commoditize the function.

items.name: EigenPal
items.tagline: AI Document Workflows for Enterprises
items.why: Document workflow automation with eval-first, on-prem and auditability addresses real enterprise trust barriers.
items.what_can_kill: Crowded document AI/RPA market and heavy customization.

items.name: Runtime
items.tagline: The AI agent harness for payment teams
items.why: Payment operations are high-value and compliance-sensitive; agents operate with approval inside customer cloud.
items.what_can_kill: Security/compliance burden and overlap with general agent platforms.

items.name: VOYGR
items.tagline: Real-world place intelligence for AI apps and agents
items.why: Clear API buyer set and freshness problem for place data; founders have direct Maps expertise.
items.what_can_kill: Google/Mapbox/data suppliers can defend distribution and data rights.

items.name: Veriad
items.tagline: AI operating system for advertising
items.why: Targets enterprises spending $50M+ on ads with regulated review workflows, giving a high-budget compliance/operations wedge.
items.what_can_kill: Enterprise sales cycle and ad-platform/incumbent convergence.

items.name: Maven
items.tagline: Payments Infrastructure for Conversational Agents
items.why: Very specific payments wall for voice/chat agents, with PCI-scope reduction and 25 gateway integrations.
items.what_can_kill: Payment processors/voice platforms can bundle the feature.

items.name: Jarmin
items.tagline: AI Employees for human-level roles
items.why: Role-level AI employee positioning ties directly to labor budget and real enterprise systems.
items.what_can_kill: Breadth across roles can make reliability/implementation non-repeatable.

items.name: Rote
items.tagline: AI-native insurance department for auto body shops
items.why: Very narrow auto-body-shop insurance workflow has a clear operational buyer and Brazil-localizable claims/authorization process.
items.what_can_kill: Public evidence found for the thesis is still thin; insurer portals/control may dominate the workflow.

items.name: BaseFrame
items.tagline: Detect what AI can automate for your team
items.why: Workflow discovery solves the upstream question before automation spend; local-data approach addresses privacy.
items.what_can_kill: May be a diagnostic feature rather than a durable system of record.

items.name: Lemma
items.tagline: Production Monitoring for AI agents
items.why: Production monitoring for agents addresses silent failures tied to churn and engineering time.
items.what_can_kill: Crowded observability category with low switching costs.

items.name: Saffron
items.tagline: Helping your company find 10x engineers.
items.why: AI-native technical assessment has a concrete hiring buyer and directly tests coding-agent usage on real code.
items.what_can_kill: Hiring-assessment market is crowded and procurement can be episodic.

items.name: Ossus
items.tagline: Intelligence for cultural institutions
items.why: Clear vertical OS for libraries plus quantified inventory/vendor/grant productivity claims and compliance posture.
items.what_can_kill: Public-sector/library budgets and sales velocity can be weak.

items.name: PumpGTM
items.tagline: Find and engage with desperate buyers across LinkedIn, Email, and X
items.why: Public customer stories show real founder-led outreach use cases across multiple teams.
items.what_can_kill: Red-ocean outbound tooling and dependency on LinkedIn/X/email policies.

items.name: Chert
items.tagline: iMessage infrastructure for business
items.why: Programmable iMessage has a crisp developer/customer-engagement wedge with API/webhooks and concrete use cases.
items.what_can_kill: Extreme Apple platform dependency and anti-abuse constraints.

items.name: Valgo
items.tagline: Insurance risk layer for physical AI
items.why: Technically credible wedge for autonomy insurance where historical claims data is scarce.
items.what_can_kill: Market timing is early and adoption depends on insurers/autonomy volume.

items.name: AgentPhone
items.tagline: Phone Numbers for AI Agents
items.why: Simple developer API for phone numbers, voice and messaging gives agents a concrete communication primitive.
items.what_can_kill: Likely feature-level moat; telecom/Twilio-like platforms can replicate.

items.name: Atrisa
items.tagline: AI Agents for Analog Circuit Design
items.why: Analog design is high-value specialized engineering; agent can save scarce expert time.
items.what_can_kill: Very technical validation and deep EDA/incumbent integration barrier.

items.name: Rubric AI
items.tagline: Reasoning and verification infra for AI
items.why: Expert reasoning/verification is a real bottleneck for high-stakes agents.
items.what_can_kill: Services/data-lab intensity and unclear recurring software buyer.
